metadata.note: The New Orleans and Northeastern Railroad (chartered 1870 from the Mandeville and Sulphur Springs RR; built 1882-83 by the Erlanger syndicate's Alabama, New Orleans, Texas and Pacific Junction Railways Co.) was the Queen & Crescent Route's 195.5-mile Meridian - New Orleans line, with no branches (ICC Valuation). Drawn as two features on identical geometry, split under Rule 4 at the late-1916 Southern Railway buyout: New Orleans and Northeastern 1883-1916, Southern Railway 1916-1970. 1970-1979 (Southern Crescent) and 1979- (Amtrak Crescent) are already drawn by southern_railway_crescent.geojson and amtrak.geojson and are deliberately not redrawn. Named trains (Q&C through service, Queen and Crescent Limited, Pelican, Southerner) are described in segment notes, not drawn separately. Report: research/branches/new_orleans_and_northeastern_railroad.txt.
sources: ICC Valuation Reports v.37 p.1 (1931), Valuation Docket 973: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:WikiProject_Trains/ICC_valuations/New_Orleans_and_Northeastern_Railroad

metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) SPLIT DATE: 1916 is a STOCK purchase (Southern bought out the remaining English-held shares, 'late 1916', month unknown); the ICC records the NO&NE operating its own road to 31 Dec 1917 and the corporation lasted to its 31 Jan 1969 merger into the AGS. By a strict 'who ran the trains' test the split could be 1917/18 or later; it should be decided once for all three Q&C roads (CNO&TP, AGS, NO&NE). When timetables switched from 'Queen & Crescent Route' to 'Southern Railway' branding is also unestablished (Q&C confirmed to Jan 1915). (2) Passenger service Meridian - Hattiesburg before the Nov 1883 through opening (sections open Oct 1882 - Jun 1883) is unproven, so 1882 is not drawn. (3) Pelican start (1941 vs post-war) and end (1969 vs 1970); Queen and Crescent Limited dates (c.1926-c.1949) not re-verified; train No. 43's extent in 1952 vs the CNO&TP report's 'Birmingham - Meridian local'. (4) Lake Pontchartrain trestle rebuild/fill dates; 203 mi of road in 1960 (Wikipedia) vs 195.528 mi (ICC). (5) Headways and speeds are estimates throughout. (6) EXISTING-LAYER DEFECT, NOT FIXED HERE: southern_railway_crescent.geojson draws the Crescent 1891-1970 over the NO&NE (Birmingham - Meridian - Hattiesburg - New Orleans), but the Crescent and its predecessors ran via Montgomery and Mobile until the 1970 Southern Crescent took the Southerner's route (Wikipedia, Southerner). Its pre-1970 geometry is the wrong alignment, and 1891-1893 'Southern Railway' is anachronistic (the Southern formed 1894). Until it is rerouted, the NO&NE corridor is drawn twice in green for 1916-1970 (and the Crescent overlies this layer's NO&NE colour for 1891-1916).
metadata.rule4_split: Feature 1 (New Orleans and Northeastern Railroad, new colour) 1883-1916; feature 2 (Southern Railway, colour pulled programmatically from the existing Southern Railway features) 1916-1970. Identical geometry.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap end to end: Meridian Union Station - New Orleans Union Passenger Terminal 202.1 mi drawn, against 195.528 mi documented for the NO&NE main line (ICC Valuation, Meridian - New Orleans) plus about 3-6 mi of New Orleans terminal trackage to UPT (Fowler mileposts: Meridian 633.5, Press St 830, Terminal Station 835.7, UPT 836.2, i.e. 202.7 mi Meridian - UPT). No approximated (straight-line) legs. Of the drawn mileage 196.9 mi runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator='Southern' (OSM names 'NS NO&NE District' / 'NO&NE District', operator Norfolk Southern); (untagged) 4.2 mi, KCS 1.0 mi, IC 0.1 mi. Traced chainage from Meridian: Meridian Union Station 0.0, Enterprise 16.2, Pachuta 26.5, Heidelberg 39.5, Laurel 56.0, Ellisville 63.9, Moselle 72.4, Hattiesburg 85.7, Purvis 101.4, Lumberton 111.9, Poplarville 124.6, Picayune 147.6, Pearl River 159.6, Slidell 167.1, North Shore 169.4, Little Woods 183.8, Gentilly yard 191.1, Back Belt Press St 193.9, Back Belt west 197.4, Back Belt / Metairie 198.2, Carrollton Ave 199.6, Union Passenger Terminal 202.1 mi, against the ICC construction sections (Pachuta 26.0, Heidelberg 39.5, Ellisville 63.0, Hattiesburg 85.0) and the Feb 1952 Guide's Table 19 mileage (Meridian 295.4 - Hattiesburg 381.0 = 85.6); the station geocodes are town centres, so chainage is good to about +-1 mi. North Shore geocoded as a hamlet ~3 mi short of Fowler's station position; it lies 0.3 km from the line. The non-Southern miles are all in New Orleans: the 'Back Belt Line' ways partly lack an old_railway_operator tag, and the last ~4 mi from the Back Belt to UPT run on the ways OSM names 'New Orleans Union Passenger Terminal' (operator Amtrak; individual ways carry old_railway_operator KCS or IC because the UPT approach tracks were jointly built). LATER-ALIGNMENT CAVEATS (Rule 2): (1) NEW ORLEANS APPROACH - the line is drawn into Union Passenger Terminal (opened 1954) via the Gentilly yard, the New Orleans Terminal Co. 'Back Belt' and the UPT approach from Carrollton Avenue. That is the post-1954 approach. For 1883-1908 trains ran instead from the lakefront along the Press Street corridor to the Q&C Press Street depot (Fowler: 'New Orleans (QC, Press St)(1883>1908)'), and for 1908-1954 from City Park Avenue to the Southern's Terminal Station at Canal and Basin streets (Fowler '(1908>1954)'). Neither earlier terminal approach was traced, so every year before 1954 is drawn on a later alignment for roughly the last 5-8 mi into New Orleans (Gentilly to the terminal). (2) LAKE PONTCHARTRAIN - the trace crosses the eastern end of the lake on the railway bridge (OSM ways 165185491 and 964655681, railway=rail bridge=yes, named 'NS NO&NE District', together 5.8 mi between North Shore and South Point; Fowler's stations are 6.4 mi apart), not a road causeway - the drawn line passes within 7 m of both bridge ends. It draws the present structure: the 1883 crossing was ~21 mi of timber trestle with two draw spans (msrailroads.com), many miles of approach trestle were later filled and the bridge rebuilt on approximately the same line; rebuild dates are not established, so 1883-era trestle geometry may differ locally. (3) Elsewhere the drawn line is the live Norfolk Southern main track; any line changes or cut-offs made between 1883 and today (not researched) are drawn in their modern form.

segments.note: New Orleans and Northeastern Railroad, operated 'by its own organization' (ICC Valuation) and marketed as part of the Queen & Crescent Route (Cincinnati Southern / AGS / NO&NE, Erlanger syndicate control). Built 1882-83; the 15 Oct 1883 train was an officials' special; first regular passenger train, the first through New Orleans - Cincinnati train, Sunday 18 Nov 1883 (Pascagoula Democrat-Star 23 Nov 1883; Magnolia Gazette 22 Nov 1883). 'Two through trains now leave New Orleans daily for Cincinnati' (St. Tammany Farmer 24 Nov 1883). Queen & Crescent through service to Cincinnati ran throughout this era. Q&C Route excursion advertising to 'all local stations' 1903 (Hattiesburg Daily Progress 19 Jun 1903) and at Meridian Jan 1915 (Hattiesburg News 12 Jan 1915). Southern Railway held a partial interest from 1895 without changing who ran the trains. Ends 1916, when the Southern bought out the English-held stock and took full control (msrailroads.com 'late 1916'; Kalmbach p.409 via Wikipedia) - a CONTROL change, not an end of service; the line continues as the Southern Railway feature. Meridian - Hattiesburg was open from Oct 1882 - Jun 1883 in stages, but no source shows passengers before Nov 1883, so 1882 is not drawn. headway_min 720 is an estimate from the two daily through trains of Nov 1883, not a counted timetable.
sources: Segment-level: opening 18 Nov 1883 from Pascagoula Democrat-Star 23 Nov 1883 and Magnolia Gazette 22 Nov 1883 (St. Tammany Farmer 24 Nov 1883 for two daily trains); Q&C service 1903 and 1915 from Hattiesburg papers; 1916 end of this era from msrailroads.com and Wikipedia/Kalmbach. Headway and speed are estimates.

properties.speed_source: estimated. The Feb 1952 Official Guide's Southern Table V (Southerner) runs Meridian 4:45 PM - New Orleans 9:10 PM, about 4 h 25 min for ~203 mi (~74 km/h for that train); locals and the Pelican were slower. 55 km/h is a blended estimate across 1916-1970, not a timetable figure. Rule 3.

segments.note: Southern Railway era (the NO&NE corporation survived as a Southern System subsidiary until merged into the Alabama Great Southern 31 Jan 1969; the ICC records it operating its own road to 31 Dec 1917, then the USRA 1918-1920). Starts at the late-1916 Southern buyout (msrailroads.com; Kalmbach p.409 via Wikipedia) - see not_yet_sourced on whether that stock purchase is the right split date. Trains: Queen & Crescent through service Cincinnati - New Orleans; the all-Pullman Queen and Crescent Limited from about 1926 (to about 1949; dates inherited from the CNO&TP research, not re-verified); the Pelican (New York - Bristol - Chattanooga - New Orleans; first-run date unresolved, 1941 photo vs 'after the war'); locals. Fowler's 1939 timetable station letter (Markwald) is a mid-era touchdown. headway_min 480 is an estimate (about three trains each way), not a counted timetable.
sources: Segment-level: 1916 start from msrailroads.com and Wikipedia/Kalmbach p.409; continuity from Fowler's 1939 timetable station letter. Individual train dates (Q&C Limited, Pelican) are NOT SOURCED at segment level and headway/speed are estimates.

segments.note: Southerner era. The streamlined Southerner (Nos. 47/48, New York - Washington - Atlanta - Birmingham - New Orleans) first ran 31 Mar 1941 and used this line via Meridian, Laurel, Hattiesburg, Picayune and Slidell. The Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 19 'Chattanooga and New Orleans (A.G.S. R.R. and N.O. & N.E. R.R.)', dated 23 Jan 1952, and Southern Tables U and V) prints legible times at Meridian, Laurel, Hattiesburg, Purvis, Lumberton, Picayune, Slidell and New Orleans for the Southerner, the Pelican (Nos. 41/42, also carrying Cincinnati - New Orleans Q&C through cars and IC-routed Shreveport sleepers) and No. 43 - three or more trains each way. Wikipedia: 13 million passenger-miles on the NO&NE in 1960. Ends 1970, when the Southerner and the Crescent were combined into the Southern Crescent on the Southerner's route; the Pelican ended 1969 or 1970 (sources conflict). The 1970-1979 Southern Crescent is drawn by southern_railway_crescent.geojson and Amtrak's Crescent from 1979 by amtrak.geojson, so this feature stops at 1970 rather than redrawing them. headway_min 480 is an estimate from the 1952 table count.
sources: Segment-level: 1941 start of the Southerner and 1970 merger into the Southern Crescent from Wikipedia (Southerner); 1951-52 service and trains from the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 19 and Southern Tables U and V (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt). Headway and speed are estimates.
